getting-started.title: Find duplicate code in VS Code

transcript.title: Your first duplicate-code review
transcript.text: Start with a small review: find repeated code, inspect its locations, and compare the copies before changing anything. Install Deslop from the VS Code Extensions panel, or use the command shown here. One extension includes the live editor experience, coding-agent checks, and the command-line tools.

transcript.title: Start with a finding
transcript.text: Open your project and a supported source file. Deslop updates its analysis as files change. The Top Offenders tree puts findings beside your code. This recording uses a real two-file C sharp example. Start with one finding so you can understand what it contains.

transcript.title: Inspect every occurrence
transcript.text: Open the finding and inspect its occurrences. A cluster groups related copies; each location lets you navigate back to the source. The canonical copy gives the comparison a consistent starting point. Read the surrounding code as well as the highlighted section before deciding what should be shared.

transcript.title: Compare before changing code
transcript.text: Compare a copy with the canonical version. Look for differences in inputs, behavior, and surrounding assumptions. A finding is evidence to review, not permission to delete code automatically. Make a focused change, run your tests, and let the live analysis update. Follow the Getting Started page for installation alternatives and command-line examples.

description.en: Install Deslop, scan a project for duplicate code, and compare two copies in the VS Code diff editor.
description.zh: 安装 Deslop，扫描项目中的重复代码，并在 VS Code 中并排比较两处副本。

transcript.title: Put policy beside your code
transcript.text: Keep shared policy in dot deslop dot toml, beside the scan root. That is the directory you ask Deslop to analyse. Use the config flag when your policy lives elsewhere. A missing configuration file uses built-in defaults, so commit your settings when the team needs consistent behavior.

transcript.title: Skip or hide?
transcript.text: Choose exclusions carefully. Exclude removes a file before analysis. Report hide still analyses the file, but hides its occurrences. A cluster disappears only when all its members are hidden. This lets a match between handwritten and generated code remain visible, without showing every generated-only cluster.

transcript.title: Override one run
transcript.text: Use command-line flags for a single run. A flag overrides its matching configuration key. Fail over supplies a duplication ceiling; no fail over clears the ceiling for that run. These options control the gate, rather than fixing or removing duplicated code.

transcript.title: Make the gate explicit
transcript.text: A threshold makes excessive duplication fail the run with exit code three. The report remains available to inspect. Without a threshold, duplication alone does not fail the scan; runtime and usage errors still can. Review the report, agree on the policy, and keep that policy with your project.

description.en: Exclude vendor files, hide generated-only findings, and set a duplicate code threshold in .deslop.toml.
description.zh: 用 .deslop.toml 排除第三方文件、隐藏仅涉及生成代码的结果，并设置重复率阈值。

ai-integration.title: Connect a coding agent to the Deslop MCP server

transcript.title: Ask before writing
transcript.text: Connect Deslop to your coding agent so it can check for existing code before writing another implementation. The key tool is find similar. Give the agent the For AI instructions linked from this page, and make the check part of its authoring workflow.

transcript.title: Use the bundled server
transcript.text: For an extension-based setup, point your MCP client at the absolute path to the server bundled inside the installed VS Code extension. Use the correct version and platform, and set the repository root. Update that path when the extension version changes. The page includes configurations for supported clients.

transcript.title: Keep the request small
transcript.text: Keep routine requests focused. Find similar checks a proposed snippet. Duplicates lists ranked findings, and cluster by ID retrieves the occurrences you need to review. Compare pair explains the evidence for two particular copies. Start with a small summary and request details only when needed.

transcript.title: Review, edit, check
transcript.text: Read any existing implementation before reusing it. After editing, run your tests and query the findings again. Deslop answers from the workspace analysis maintained by the editor, which refreshes as files change. The agent still needs to inspect behavior and decide whether a suggested reuse is appropriate.

description.en: Configure the Deslop MCP server for a coding agent and query the workspace for duplicate code before editing.
description.zh: 为编程智能体配置 Deslop MCP 服务器，在编辑前查询工作区中的重复代码。

how-it-works.title: How Deslop finds copied and similar code

transcript.title: From source to findings
transcript.text: Deslop parses source code with tree sitter, finds candidate copies, checks their content, and groups the surviving findings. The editor, command-line tools and MCP share a Rust engine. A live session refreshes after edits; a command-line scan is a separate review of its selected input.

transcript.title: Structure is a starting point
transcript.text: Syntax-tree normalization helps find copies despite changed names, literals or formatting. But normalization alone cannot establish a clone. Deslop also checks shared content, consistent renaming and the operations being performed. Matching structure is a starting point for comparison, rather than proof on its own.

transcript.title: Read the category
transcript.text: Read the finding category before acting. Identical, nearly identical and similar code describe different degrees of copying. Same shape with different content is informational and contributes nothing to clone counts. Optional embedding candidates also need review: similarity does not prove interchangeable behavior or a safe extraction.

transcript.title: Size is not confidence
transcript.text: Duplicated mass combines syntax-tree size with additional visible copies, bringing larger repeated work to the top. It is neither confidence nor a percentage. The duplication percentage counts covered source lines, counting overlaps once. Compare two explicit occurrences to inspect their evidence before making a change.

description.en: See why renamed variables can still produce a match and how Deslop ranks duplicate code by the amount copied.
description.zh: 了解变量改名后为何仍能找到副本，以及 Deslop 如何按重复规模排序。

transcript.title: Three syntax flavors
transcript.text: Osprey has three syntax flavors. Deslop documents native braces and ML support, plus explicit selection for Osprey Python. This page describes the development integration, so check your installed release before expecting every change. Ordinary Python files should keep their own language identity.

transcript.title: Choose Python deliberately
transcript.text: For an Osprey Python source file, put the flavor marker in a leading source comment. The same words inside a string, or in a comment after code, do not select the flavor. This makes language selection deliberate instead of treating every Python file as Osprey.

transcript.title: Use the project manifest
transcript.text: The project manifest can also select the Python entry file and individual Python sources. These are literal file paths relative to the manifest, not directory-wide patterns. Other Python files remain ordinary Python. Project flavor overrides and nested project rules are described in the page.

transcript.title: Review the actual copies
transcript.text: Open the project with Deslop or scan it from the command line. Review the ranked findings and compare their occurrences before extracting shared code. Language support does not promise automatic Osprey refactoring, cross-flavor equivalence, or interchangeable behavior. Invalid ML syntax should surface as a parse error.

description.en: Scan Osprey code and see how a Python flavor marker or osprey.toml selects files for analysis.
description.zh: 扫描 Osprey 代码，并了解如何通过 Python 语法标记或 osprey.toml 选择要分析的文件。

github-action.title: Check duplicate code in GitHub Actions

transcript.title: Put review in the workflow
transcript.text: The Deslop GitHub Action brings duplicate-code review into your workflow. It installs the released command-line tool, analyses the workspace and renders reports. Start with the complete workflow on the documentation page, including repository checkout, and choose whether you want measurement or a blocking gate.

transcript.title: Pin the release
transcript.text: Pin an exact release tag. By default, that tag selects the matching command-line version, keeping the action and tool aligned. If you pin a commit or branch instead, supply the version input explicitly. The downloaded archive is checked against its published checksum before extraction.

transcript.title: Measure, then choose a ceiling
transcript.text: For a measurement-only run, use no fail over. To make duplication above your ceiling fail the job, set fail over, or leave it unset to honor the project configuration. The five-percent value shown is an example, not a recommendation for every codebase. Review your baseline first.

transcript.title: Understand the gate scope
transcript.text: Changed-code gating uses a supplied patch and the only changed option. The whole tree is still analysed; the report and gate are scoped to affected added lines. Reports and outputs help explain a breached gate. Inspect the scope as well as the percentage before deciding what to change.

description.en: Add Deslop to GitHub Actions and fail a pull request check when the duplicate code percentage exceeds a threshold.
description.zh: 在 GitHub Actions 中运行 Deslop，当代码重复率超过阈值时让拉取请求检查失败。

vscode-cluster-panel.title: Compare duplicate code side by side in VS Code

transcript.title: Open the occurrence
transcript.text: Open a finding and use its file links to navigate to the code. The selected range shows the reported occurrence, but read the surrounding implementation too. The category tells you what kind of relationship was found. A finding is a starting point for review.

transcript.title: Compare against a reference
transcript.text: Compare To Canonical opens the reference occurrence on the left and your chosen copy on the right. Canonical does not mean best. It gives comparisons a consistent starting point. Review both implementations and their assumptions before deciding which behavior to preserve.

transcript.title: Choose another pair
transcript.text: To inspect a different pair, select the first occurrence for comparison, then choose Compare with Selected on the other. Clear Selection cancels the choice. Selection also clears after comparison or when you change clusters. Copy Context For AI provides finding context for a coding agent.

transcript.title: Read the numbers correctly
transcript.text: Mass measures copied syntax-tree size multiplied by additional visible copies. Rank puts larger duplicated work first; neither is confidence. Severity is a configured diagnostic level. Use the sidebar grouping menu to organize findings, and the Duplication and Session views to inspect percentages and analysis state.

description.en: Jump to each copy from a Deslop finding and compare any two occurrences in the VS Code diff editor.
description.zh: 从 Deslop 的结果跳转到每处副本，并在 VS Code 的差异编辑器中比较任意两处。

accuracy-transparency.title: How to read code duplication percentages

transcript.title: Percentage is not accuracy
transcript.text: Duplication percentage tells you how much analysed source is covered by reported clones. It does not tell you how accurate the detector is. A false positive can inflate the percentage, and a missed clone can reduce it. Correct arithmetic does not establish correct detection.

transcript.title: Count covered lines once
transcript.text: Analysed lines include physical source lines, including blanks and comments. Duplicated lines are the union of visible clone ranges within each file, so overlaps count once. Hidden occurrences do not enter the numerator, while their analysed files remain in the denominator. Excluded files leave analysis entirely.

transcript.title: Check known examples
transcript.text: Accuracy checks use judged source pairs pinned to repository commits. Clearly in identifies a known clone; clearly out identifies a pair that should not be reported. Unclear cases assert neither verdict. Range coverage separately asks whether the report covers the whole judged copy rather than just a small fragment.

transcript.title: Interpret the gate
transcript.text: The gate fails when the full-precision percentage is greater than its ceiling. Equality passes, even if display rounding makes nearby values look identical. Read the report scope and the measured build together. Corpus results apply to judged examples; they do not guarantee perfect precision or recall everywhere.

description.en: Learn which lines count toward a duplicate code percentage and how Deslop checks its findings against known examples.
description.zh: 了解哪些代码行计入重复率，以及 Deslop 如何用已知示例检验检测结果。

research-background.title: Types of duplicate code and how to detect them

transcript.title: Why repeated code matters
transcript.text: Repeated code is not automatically wrong. The maintenance risk is that fixes, security changes and new behavior must stay consistent across copies. Generating another implementation is easy; deciding whether to reuse existing code still requires judgment. The research page links the studies behind this motivation.

transcript.title: Four families of clones
transcript.text: The research taxonomy distinguishes four clone families. Type one permits layout and comment changes. Type two allows changed names and literals. Type three includes edited statements. Type four describes equivalent behavior implemented differently. Deslop has its own report labels and a stricter text-identity rule, explained in How It Works.

transcript.title: Combine several techniques
transcript.text: Deslop combines normalized syntax trees, subtree fingerprints, statement-run fingerprints and similarity retrieval. Optional embeddings add semantic candidates. These techniques help locate possible copies at different levels. Pair admission checks content as well as structure, and an explicit comparison provides evidence about the selected source ranges.

transcript.title: Evidence still needs review
transcript.text: Use the page to follow implementation pointers and read the original papers. A detection technique is not proof that extracting shared code is safe. Review both implementations, test the behavior you intend to keep, and use the separate accuracy documentation to understand how findings are checked.

description.en: Compare exact copies, renamed copies, and edited copies, and see what makes a similar code finding worth reviewing.
description.zh: 对比完全相同、改名和改动过的代码副本，了解哪些相似代码值得审查。

for-ai.title: Find similar code before writing with an AI coding agent

transcript.title: Verify the session first
transcript.text: Before working in a new codebase, inspect the installed tool version and available tool parameters. Bind MCP to the absolute repository root, read the project instructions and configuration, then call session and verify its root. A connection to another repository is not a useful empty result.

transcript.title: Small summaries, all occurrences
transcript.text: Request duplicates with detail summary and a small limit. Scope edits with path or path_contains, then use cluster-by-id and inspect every member, paging with offset, before editing. Keep overview pages small: full occurrences for one cluster, not hundreds of full clusters.

transcript.title: find-similar before writing
transcript.text: Before adding a code unit, call find similar with a snippet and its language. Inspect clusters and also existing occurrences outside any cluster. An existing match still needs review, even when clusters is empty. A disk report cannot answer this in-memory snippet query.

transcript.title: Tests, then requery
transcript.text: After editing, run the project's tests and query the changed paths again. The live index refreshes automatically; use rescan only for suspected watcher lag. A merge plan is optional. A verdict asking for agent or human judgment is not an executable merge.

description.en: Use the Deslop MCP find-similar tool to find reusable code in the live workspace, then test and check again after editing.
description.zh: 通过 Deslop MCP 的 find-similar 工具查找工作区中可复用的代码，并在修改后测试和复查。
